name: ssh
summary: Connects securely to a remote machine.
description: Opens an encrypted shell on a remote server, or runs a command there. Authentication uses a password or, preferably, a key (ssh-keygen then ssh-copy-id). Host aliases are configured in ~/.ssh/config.

options.description: Private key to use for authentication.
Local port forwarding: -L 8080:localhost:80 makes the remote port 80 available on local port 8080.
Remote port forwarding: exposes a local port on the server.
Goes through a jump host (bastion) before reaching the host.
One-off configuration option, for example -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no.
Verbose mode, to troubleshoot a connection problem (-vvv for more detail).

example.output:
debug1: Connecting to server.com [51.15.0.12] port 22.
debug1: Authenticating with public key "/home/esprit/.ssh/id_ed25519"

options.description: Runs no remote command (useful for plain port forwarding).
Enables X11 forwarding to run remote graphical applications.

arguments.name: USER@HOST
arguments.description: Account and address (domain name, IP or alias from ~/.ssh/config).

arguments.name: COMMAND
arguments.description: Command to run remotely instead of opening a shell.

examples.explanation: Opens a shell on the machine 192.168.1.20 with the esprit account.
Connects with a specific private key.
Runs df -h remotely and shows the result locally.
Reaches the server’s PostgreSQL database locally through a tunnel.
